item.title: SXSW London 2026: AEG’s Alex Hill Says U.K. Live Industry Wants to Move ‘Quicker’ Than Government on Ticket Resale Legislation
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest trends and discussions in the music industry. Today, we're talking about the challenges of ticket sales and the live music scene. Joining us are insights from Alex Hill, President and CEO of AEG International, who recently spoke at SXSW London. Let's dive in."
[Soft music transition]
Host: "Hill discussed the issue of secondary ticket markets selling tickets above face value, a problem that's been plaguing fans for decades. The UK government had promised to ban this practice, but legislation has been delayed, leaving artists and industry leaders frustrated."
[Short audio clip from Alex Hill's speech] Alex Hill: "I think as an industry we'd like to work quicker than the regulator at the moment. But it will always be an issue... There's a number of bad actors, such as bots and touts that will look to make that process even tougher."
Host: "Hill also touched on the growth of the live music scene, which has seen a post-pandemic boom. While growth has slowed down recently, he credits the streaming and digital market for introducing fans to new genres and artists. This summer, fans can look forward to shows by Bad Bunny and BTS at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London."
[Soft music transition]
Host: "Despite the demand for live music, Hill notes that costs are a major concern for promoters and venues. With rising taxes and labor costs, the industry needs to be careful not to let costs impact demand. As Hill put it, 'demand is not a problem in our industry,' but managing costs is crucial to keeping the live music scene thriving."
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for today's podcast. Thanks for tuning in to our discussion on the live music industry and the challenges of ticket sales. We'll be back with more insights and trends in the music world."
